summary: Examples of #AnsibleRequires imports for core, collection, relative and optional PowerShell and C# utils; optional imports must be checked in code, and #AnsibleRequires is preferred over #Requires -Module.
questions: How do I import a PowerShell module util from my collection?
How do I import a util from the same collection using a relative name?

answer_card.title: #AnsibleRequires import examples
answer_card.answer_md:
```powershell
#AnsibleRequires -PowerShell Ansible.ModuleUtils.Legacy
#AnsibleRequires -PowerShell ansible_collections.my_namespace.my_name.plugins.module_utils.my_util
#AnsibleRequires -PowerShell ..module_utils.my_util
#AnsibleRequires -PowerShell Ansible.ModuleUtils.Optional -Optional
#AnsibleRequires -CSharpUtil Ansible.Process
#AnsibleRequires -CSharpUtil ..module_utils.my_util
```
With `-Optional`, check that a function/type exists before using it. Prefer `#AnsibleRequires` over `#Requires -Module`: it supports collections, relative names and optional imports.
